title: Remove default admin user and create one with other name
description: Before deploying any new FortiGate, it is important to change the password of the default admin account. It is also recommended that you change even the user name of the default admin account, However, since you cannot change the user name of an account that is currently in use, a second administrator account must be created in order to do this. FAILs if the default 'admin' account still exists. Logging in as admin with a blank password (the CIS audit) is also worth trying. Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.4.1 Remove default admin user and create one with other name

remediation.command:
config system admin
    edit "mycompanyadmin"
        set accprofile "super_admin"
        set password <password>
    next
end
(log in as mycompanyadmin, then)
config system admin
    delete "admin"
end
# CIS guidance:
First create an other local admin account, for example mycompanyadmin.
#if VDOM enabled
config global
#configure new admin
config system admin
    edit "mycompanyadmin"
        set password
        set accprofile "super_admin"
    next
end
Verify if the newly created login works by opening another CLI session, do not logout of your current session. Once validated, logout with the default local admin account and use the CLI session with mycompanyadmin to delete the default local admin account. Please make sure there are no references in the configuration to the account (groups, etc.)
#if VDOM enabled
config global
    config system admin
        delete "admin"
    end
To change the default password in the GUI:
Global (if VDOM enabled) > System > Administrators Create New admin account (mycompanyadmin) Verify if you can login with that account via another browser session (eg. incognito mode). Remove default admin System > Administrators menu

title: Ensure the latest firmware is installed
description: Check against the Fortinet website to make sure that the latest stable firmware is installed.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.1.6 Ensure the latest firmware is installed

audit.command: First, check for the latest firmware version available by going to https://docs.fortinet.com/upgrade-tool, select your product from the Current Product drop-down menu, then select the upgrade to FortiOS Version for the latest available version. Second, verify the current firmware on your system. In the CLI: get system status ... Version: Fortigate-100D v6.2.7,build1190,201216 (GA) ... In the GUI: 1. Go to Dashboard > Status > System information 2. Check for firmware. (Full steps: CIS 2.1.6.)

remediation.command:
First, determine the upgrade path recommended by Fortinet. If you have not upgraded the system for a long time, it is not recommended to upgrade straight to the latest version, as the configuration could be lost. Fortinet provides a tool to recommend an upgrade path for all of its products. Go to https://docs.fortinet.com/upgrade-tool. Choose your product from the "Current Product" drop-down menu, the "current FortiOS version", and the latest firmware version available for that model from "Upgrade to FortiOS Version". Click "Go". Write down the path and then click on "Download" to download all the necessary versions. The second step is to download the required FortiOS firmware/s. Go to https://support.fortinet.com and login. Go to Support -> Firmware Download. Once there, select the product and click on "Upgrade Path". Choose the specific model of the hardware, the current firmware version and the latest firmware version available for that model. Click "Go". Write down the path and then click on "Download" to download all the necessary versions. The last step is to install the new firmwares in the order provided by the "Upgrade tool". It is recommended to use GUI to perform this task as it would be much easier. In the GUI
1. Go to System > Fabric Management
2. Right click on device that needs to be upgraded.
3. Then click on "Upgrade". You might have to perform this step multiple times if you follow the upgrade path.

title: Ensure 'Password Policy' is enabled
description: It is important to use secure and complex passwords for preventing unauthorized access to the FortiGate device. PASS requires the password policy enabled, applied to admin-password and minimum-length 14 or more. Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.2.1 Ensure 'Password Policy' is enabled

remediation.command:
config system password-policy
    set status enable
    set apply-to admin-password ipsec-preshared-key
    set minimum-length 14
end
# CIS guidance:
Can be modified from CLI or GUI. From CLI, do the following:
config system password-policy
    set status enable
    set apply-to admin-password ipsec-preshared-key
    set minimum-length 14
end
Or from GUI, do the following:
1) Log in to FortiGate as Super Admin
2) Go to 'System' > 'Settings'
3) Find the 'Password Policy' section
4) Default 'Password scope' is 'Off', change it to 'Both'
5) set 'Minimum length' to '14'

title: Ensure administrator password retries and lockout time are configured
description: Failed login attempts can indicate malicious attempts to gain access to your network. To prevent this security risk, FortiGate is preconfigured to limit the number of failed administrator login attempts. After the maximum number of failed login attempts is reached, access to the account is blocked for the configured lockout period. PASS requires admin-lockout-threshold of 3 or less and admin-lockout-duration of 900 seconds or less, exactly as the CIS audit states (the CIS remediation value is 900). Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.2.2 Ensure administrator password retries and lockout time are configured

remediation.command:
config system global
    set admin-lockout-threshold 3
    set admin-lockout-duration 900
end
# CIS guidance:
To configure the lockout options, from CLI:
config system global
    set admin-lockout-threshold 3
    set admin-lockout-duration 900
end
Lockout affects the offending IP address, not the entire account.

title: Ensure only SNMPv3 is enabled
description: Ensuring that only SNMPv3 service is enabled and SNMPv1, SNMPv2c are disabled. PASS requires the SNMP agent enabled, an empty config system snmp community block (no v1/v2c communities) and at least one SNMPv3 user. Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.3.1 Ensure only SNMPv3 is enabled

audit.pattern:
(?ms)^config system snmp sysinfo
(?:[ 	]+[^
]*
)*?[ 	]+set status enable[ 	]*
.*?^config system snmp community
end[ 	]*$.*?^config system snmp user
[ 	]+edit

remediation.command:
config system snmp sysinfo
    set status enable
end
config system snmp community
    delete <id>
end
config system snmp user
    edit "snmp_v3"
        set security-level auth-priv
        set auth-proto sha256
        set auth-pwd <password>
        set priv-proto aes256
        set priv-pwd <password>
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To enable SNMP agent in CLI:
config system snmp sysinfo
    set status enable
end
In GUI, go to System > SNMP and enable SNMP Agent. To delete SNMPv1/2c communities. In this example, we'll delete community "public" in CLI:
First, to identify the community, run
config system snmp community
    show
    config system snmp community
        edit 1
            set name "public"
            config hosts
                edit 1
                next
            end
        next
    end
This shows that the community public has ID 1
config system snmp community
    delete 1
end
In the GUI, go to:
System > SNMP, select the community and click on the Delete button. To add SNMPv3 user in CLI:
config system snmp user
    edit "snmp_test"
        set security-level auth-priv
        set auth-proto sha256
        set auth-pwd xxxx
        set priv-proto aes256
        set priv_pwd xxxx
    end
In the GUI, go to:
1. System > SNMP, under SNMPv3, click on "Create New" button.
2. Select "Authentication" and choose SHA256 as Authentication algorithm.
3. Click "Change" to type in the password.
4. Also select option "Private", choose AES256 as Encryption Algorithm.
5. Click on "Change" to change the password. Click "OK" to add the new user.
6. Click apply to apply the new setting into the current config.

title: Allow only trusted hosts in SNMPv3
description: Ensuring that only certain hosts are able to conduct SNMP GET or receive SNMP Trap. FAILs if any SNMPv3 user lists 0.0.0.0 in notify-hosts. Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.3.2 Allow only trusted hosts in SNMPv3

remediation.command:
config system snmp user
    edit "<user>"
        unselect notify-hosts 0.0.0.0
        set notify-hosts <nms-ip>
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To remove 0.0.0.0 from trusted hosts in CLI:
config system snmp user
    edit "snmp_test"
        unselect notify-hosts 0.0.0.0
    end
From GUI:
1. System > SNMP.
2. On SNMPv3 section, double click on the configured SNMPv3 settings.
3. Remove 0.0.0.0 from "Hosts" option.

title: Ensure all the login accounts having specific trusted hosts enabled
description: Configure an administrative account to be accessible only to someone who is using a trusted host. You can set a specific IP address for the trusted host or use a subnet. FAILs if any administrator still has the default trusthost1 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 (no trusted host restriction). Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.4.2 Ensure all the login accounts having specific trusted hosts enabled

remediation.command:
config system admin
    edit "<admin>"
        set trusthost1 10.0.0.0 255.255.255.0
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To remove a trusted host item from the list in CLI:
config system admin
    edit "test_admin"
        unset trusthost1
    end
To add a trusted host into the list in CLI:
config system admin
    edit "test_admin"
        set trusthost6 1.1.1.1 255.255.255.255
    end
Before adding an item, please make sure that it does not already exist. For example, if trusthost3 is already in the list, using it again will override the existing host/network. In the Web GUI:
1. System > Administrators.
2. select the account and click on edit.
3. In the account setting page, make sure that "Restrict login to trusted hosts" is enabled and all the allowed hosts / subnets are in the list of trusted host. Please take note that certain versions of FortiOS will only show the first 3 trusted hosts in the list. If you want to see more, you have to click on the "+" sign as if you're adding a new item into the list. Keep clicking until you see an empty field of trusted host. That's when you know that you have reached the bottom of the list. To add another trusted host, fill in the empty field of the new "Trusted Host". To remove a trusted host, simply erase everything in the field of that corresponding host.

title: Ensure only encrypted access channels are enabled
description: Allow only HTTPS access to the GUI and SSH access to the CLI. FAILs if any interface allowaccess list contains http or telnet. Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.4.5 Ensure only encrypted access channels are enabled

remediation.command:
config system interface
    edit "port1"
        set allowaccess ssh https ping snmp
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
If HTTP or Telnet is in the allowaccess list, you will have to set that list again with the same elements except for http or telnet. On CLI:
config system interface
    edit port1
        set allowaccess ssh https ping snmp
    end
In the web GUI, click on:
1. Network > Interfaces, select the interface and click "Edit".
2. In the interface setting page, uncheck HTTP and Telnet in the section "Administrative Access".

title: Ensure that policies do not use "ALL" as Service
description: Ensure that all security policies in effect clearly state which protocols / services they are allowing. FAILs if an accept policy uses the "ALL" service (deny policies such as the CIS 3.3 ISDB rules may use ALL). Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 3.2 Ensure that policies do not use "ALL" as Service

remediation.command:
config firewall policy
    edit <id>
        set service "HTTPS" "DNS"
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
This is an example showing how to modify policy with ID of 2 to change the service from "ALL" to FTP and SNMP. In CLI:
config firewall policy
    edit 2
        set service "FTP" "SNMP"
    end
In the GUI,
1. Go to Policy & Objects.
2. Click on Firewall Policy.
3. Select the policy, click "Edit".
4. In the Service section, click on it and select FTP and SNMP. Click OK.

title: Ensure firewall policy denying all traffic to/from Tor, malicious server, or scanner IP addresses using ISDB
description: Firewall policies should include a deny rule for traffic going to/from Tor, malicious server, or scanner IP addresses using ISDB (Internet Service Database). PASS requires a policy using ISDB source Tor-Exit.Node (inbound) and a policy using ISDB destination Tor-Relay.Node (outbound); confirm both list all CIS ISDB objects and use action deny with logging. Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 3.3 Ensure firewall policy denying all traffic to/from Tor, malicious server, or scanner IP addresses using ISDB

remediation.command:
config firewall policy
    edit 0
        set name "Block-Malicious-In"
        set srcintf "any"
        set dstintf "any"
        set internet-service-src enable
        set internet-service-src-name "Tor-Exit.Node" "Tor-Relay.Node" "Censys-Scanner" "Shodan-Scanner" "Botnet-C&C.Server" "Phishing-Phishing.Server" "Proxy-Proxy.Server" "Spam-Spamming.Server" "VPN-Anonymous.VPN" "Malicious-Malicious.Server"
        set dstaddr "all"
        set action deny
        set schedule "always"
        set service "ALL"
        set logtraffic all
    next
    edit 0
        set name "Block-Malicious-Out"
        set srcintf "any"
        set dstintf "any"
        set srcaddr "all"
        set internet-service enable
        set internet-service-name "Tor-Relay.Node" "Botnet-C&C.Server" "Phishing-Phishing.Server" "Proxy-Proxy.Server" "Spam-Spamming.Server" "VPN-Anonymous.VPN" "Malicious-Malicious.Server"
        set action deny
        set schedule "always"
        set logtraffic all
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
Review firewall policies and ensure there are:
1. A firewall policy created to block inbound connections with these settings:
From: Any To: Any Source: "Tor-Exit.Node", "Tor-Relay.Node", "Censys-Scanner", "Shodan- Scanner", "Botnet-C&C.Server", "Phishing-Phishing.Server", "Proxy- Proxy.Server", "Spam-Spamming.Server", "VPN-Anonymous.VPN", and "Malicious- Malicious.Server" Destination: all Schedule: Always Services: All Action: Deny Log Violation Traffic: Enabled Enable this policy: Enabled
2. A firewall policy created to block outbound connections with these settings:
From: Any To: Any Source: All Destination: "Tor-Relay.Node", "Botnet-C&C.Server", "Phishing- Phishing.Server", "Proxy-Proxy.Server", "Spam-Spamming.Server", "VPN- Anonymous.VPN", and "Malicious-Malicious.Server" Schedule: Always Action: Deny Log Violation Traffic: Enabled Enable this policy: Enabled

title: Detect Botnet connections
description: Interfaces which are classified as "WAN" and are used by a policy should use an IPS sensor which blocks or monitors outgoing connections to botnet sites. PASS requires an IPS sensor with scan-botnet-connections block; confirm it is applied to all WAN-bound policies. Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 4.1.1 Detect Botnet connections

remediation.command:
config ips sensor
    edit "<sensor>"
        set scan-botnet-connections block
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
On GUI:
1. Configure relevant IPS profiles with "Scan Outgoing Connections to Botnet Sites" set to "Block".
2. Apply relevant IPS profile on all firewall policies with traffic exiting the network to a "WAN" interface.

        next

end
# CIS guidance:
Local-in Policies can only be configured through the CLI:
config firewall {local-in-policy | local-in-policy6}
    edit <policy_number>
        set intf <interface>
        set srcaddr <source_address> [source_address] ...
        set dstaddr <destination_address> [destination_address] ...

title: Ensure default Admin ports are changed
description: FortiGate admin ports listen on the common ports of 80 and 443. This is default behavior. While interface access is controlled by configuring network interfaces, the FortiGate still listens on the admin ports that have been configured, which can also cause a conflict should 80 or 443 be needed as part of additional configuration later on. FAILs if admin-port is still 80 or admin-sport is still 443 (admin-https-redirect must also be disabled when port 80 is changed). Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.4.7 Ensure default Admin ports are changed

remediation.command:
config system global
    set admin-https-redirect disable
    set admin-port 8082
    set admin-sport 4343
end
# CIS guidance:
config system global
    set admin-https-redirect disable
    set admin-port 8082 **(or any other uncommon port)**
    set admin-server-cert "self-sign"
    set admin-sport 4343 **(or any other uncommon port)**
end
OR From Web GUI:
1. System > Settings
2. Change the ports/settings under 'Administration Settings' section. NOTE: https redirection must be turned off as well as changing port 80. This is due to the nature of how browser port redirection works. The browser will be redirected from port 80 to port 443 or whichever 'admin-sport' is configured, meaning that it will still listen on port 80 even when the port has been reconfigured.

title: Ensure Security Fabric is Configured
description: Ensure Root FortiGate is configured as security fabric root.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 5.2.1.1 Ensure Security Fabric is Configured

remediation.command:

title: Apply a Trusted Signed Certificate for VPN Portal
description: Apply a signed certificate from a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) to the SSL VPN portal to allow users to connect securely with confidence. FAILs if the SSL VPN still uses the factory self-signed certificate (Fortinet_Factory). Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 6.1.1 Apply a Trusted Signed Certificate for VPN Portal

remediation.command:
config vpn ssl settings
    set servercert "<trusted-cert>"
end
# CIS guidance:
Import a signed certificate from a trusted CA through the GUI:
1. Go to System > Certificates > Import.
2. Then assign the certificate to the SSL VPN portal by going to VPN > SSL- VPN Settings and selecting the proper certificate in the dropdown for "Server Certificate".

title: Enable Event Logging

title: Ensure DNS server is configured
description: Fortinet uses the Domain Name Service (DNS) to translate host names into IP addresses. To enable DNS lookups, you must specify the primary DNS server for your system. You can also specify secondary and tertiary DNS servers. When resolving host names, the system consults the primary name server. If a failure or time-out occurs, the system consults the secondary name server. For security purpose, trusted DNS servers should be configured to prevent man-in-the- middle attacks. PASS requires a primary DNS server in config system dns. Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.1 Ensure DNS server is configured

remediation.command:
config system dns
    set primary 8.8.8.8
    set secondary 8.8.4.4
end
# CIS guidance:
In this example, we will assign 8.8.8.8 as primary DNS and 8.8.4.4 as secondary DNS. In CLI:
config system dns
    set primary 8.8.8.8
    set secondary 8.8.4.4
end
In the GUI, go to Networks > DNS. Click on "Specify" and put in 8.8.8.8 as "Primary DNS Server" and 8.8.4.4 as "Secondary DNS Server"

end

title: Ensure timezone is properly configured
description: Sets the local time zone information so that the time displayed by the device is more relevant to those who are viewing it.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.1.3 Ensure timezone is properly configured

audit.command: In the CLI, do the following command and check the result of timezone filed in the output get system global ... timezone : (GMT-8:00) Pacific Time (US & Canada) ... Or from GUI, do the following: 1) Login to FortiGate 2) Go to 'System' -> 'Settings'. 3) Time Zone and NTP settings are under 'System Time'

remediation.command:
In this example, we will set Eastern Timezone (GMT-5:00) for the Fortigate. Each timezone will have its corresponding ID. To find the correct ID, when you type in the command "set timezone ", also type the question mark '?' to list all of the available timezones and their IDs. The ID of the Eastern Timezone is 12 In the CLI:
config system global
    set timezone 12
end
In the GUI, do the following:
1) After login to fortigate, go to 'System' -> 'Settings'
2) Select '(GMT-5:00) Eastern Time (US & Canada)' under 'System Time'

title: Enabling SNMP trap for memory usage
description: Enabling SNMP traps for memory usage monitoring helps detect anomalies and ensure critical security features remain operational. This proactive approach enhances system reliability by alerting administrators to potential resource issues. PASS requires trap-free-memory-threshold 20 and trap-freeable-memory-threshold 50 (the CIS values). Audited against FortiOS 'show full-configuration' output (run it from the global context on VDOM-enabled units and save the full output); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiGate 7.4.x Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.3.4 Enabling SNMP trap for memory usage

    set status enable
    set trap-free-memory-threshold 20
    set trap-freeable-memory-threshold 50
end
# CIS guidance:
To configure SNMP trap trap-free-memory-threshold and trap-freeable-memory- threshold. From CLI:
config system snmp sysinfo
    show
    config system snmp sysinfo
        set status enable
        set trap-free-memory-threshold 20
        set trap-freeable-memory-threshold 50
    end
